'''William Gerard Dwyer''' (born 1947) is an American  [[mathematician]] specializing in [[algebraic topology]] and [[group theory]]. For many years he was a professor at the [[University of Notre Dame]], where he is the William J. Hank Family Professor Emeritus.

== Life ==

He was born in 1947 in [[Jersey City, New Jersey]].

== Career ==

Dwyer completed his [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] at [[Boston College]] in 1969.<ref name="homepage">{{cite web|url=https://math.nd.edu/people/emeritus/william-g-dwyer/|title=Home Page at the University of Notre Dame|access-date=2018-05-15|archive-date=2018-01-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128084803/http://math.nd.edu/people/emeritus/william-g-dwyer/}}</ref>

He completed his [[Ph.D.]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1973. His doctoral thesis was on ''Strong Convergence of the Eilenberg-Moore Spectral Sequence'' and his doctoral advisor was [[Daniel Marinus Kan|Daniel Kan]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|12975}}</ref> Afterwards he taught at [[Yale University]] and visited the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]] before joining the faculty at  the [[University of Notre Dame]].<ref name="honorary">{{cite web|url=https://www.uw.edu.pl/wp-content/uploads/2014/05/Dwyer.pdf|title=William G. Dwyer, Doctor Honoris Causa}}</ref>

In 1998 Dwyer was an [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Berlin]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Dwyer, William G.|chapter=Lie groups and ''p''-compact groups|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians|volume=2|pages=433–442|year=1998|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011699000}}</ref> In 2007 he was awarded a [[honorary degree|Doctor Honoris Causa degree]] by the [[University of Warsaw]].<ref name="honorary" />  He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2012.  He is currently emeritus professor of mathematics at the University of Notre Dame.<ref name="homepage"/>
